Je me suis laissée tenter par Prey après en avoir entendu grandement parler, quand je dis après, c’est bien quelques années après. Son côté spatial et horrifique m’ont beaucoup attirés, alors même que les deux me font flipper comme jamais. Le vide sous toutes ses formes me fait flipper (hauteur, espace vide d’air, etc…). Mais la peur ne m’empêche pas d’être également fascinée par ce qui se trouve si loin de nous. Ce jeu n’est pas un survival game, même s’il faudra tout de même récupérer pas mal d’objets régulièrement.

Ce qui m’avait tenté également c’est que le jeu a été développé par Arkane Studio, qui est également à l’origine des Dishonored, une franchise que j’affectionne beaucoup également pour son univers sombre. On peut dire que les jeux avec une ambiance bien sombre, ça les connais ! D’ailleurs, notre personnage peut acquérir un pouvoir similaire à celui dans Dishonored et qui nous permet de nous « téléporter » d’un point à un autre. L’intrigue commence comme si tout allait très bien, une grande cinématique finie même par avoir lieu pour nous faire un petit tour un peu comique de la zone… ou plutôt, de l’endroit où l’on croit être… Très vite, la réalité s’est avérée bien différente de cette cinématique, bien plus horrifique et stressante. En tant que joueuse, je me suis retrouvée aussi perdue que le personnage en lui-même qui ne comprend pas bien ce qui lui arrive. Il refait alors le même trajet pour sortir de sa chambre et aller à la zone de test, la surprise est de taille. Tout ce qu’il a vu n’était alors qu’une simulation ! Le cauchemar commence et semble ne jamais vouloir cesser. On rencontre plus de cadavres que d’êtres vivants, mais il en reste malgré tout, il ne tient alors qu’à nous de les sauver ou non. Par contre, aucun d’entre eux ne deviendra un allié potentiel, on se contente de les sauver et c’est tout. Certains deviendront comme des assistants, même s’ils restent inutiles, leur vrai visage s’ouvrira lors de la fin de l’histoire d’ailleurs. Le jeu propose plusieurs fins suivant nos choix et franchement, cette fin elle me donne envie d’une suite liée à ce qu’on nous montre… Les différentes armes sont impressionnantes et avec des capacités propres, certaines servent juste à déverrouiller des portes (l’arbalète jouet). Il devait faire bon vivre au sein de la station lorsqu’elle était fonctionnelle, mais ce genre de structure montre aussi vite ses limites face aux situations d’urgences (surtout quand on s’amuse à manipuler l’inconnu).

Les graphismes sont plutôt pas mal à mon sens, j’adore le design des différents ennemis du jeu. La musique se prête bien à l’ambiance horrifique également et il n’est pas évident de s’orienter dans le complexe spatiale. Les sorties dans l’espace sont assez complexes à prendre en mains et à l’intérieur c’est encore pire (pour l’orientation). Le jeu parvient vraiment à faire perdre les repaires c’est fou (bon après, c’est le premier jeu spatial que je fais). Pour l’intérieur, avec la gravité, le gameplay est identique à d’autres FPS, on a une roue des armes, mais aussi des compétences. On a des points de vie, une barrière et ensuite une barre qui s’ajoute pour les capacités Typhons. Les items à récupérer sont nombreux et pas toujours évidents à trouver, souvent liés à des quêtes. Il faut aussi retrouver tous les membres de la station, mort comme vif, ce qui peut prendre du temps. Il est possible de suivre ceux que l’on a trouvé via les PC disséminés dans le jeu (et qui servent à d’autres choses aussi). On peut faire du piratage également. Le jeu est vraiment complet et si Steam ne bugué pas, je pourrais mieux définir le temps que j’ai passé dessus. Je trouve le jeu vraiment très complet et prenant, malgré son côté angoissant. Les jeux d’horreurs ne sont généralement pas mon truc, mais pour celui-ci ça va. C’est vraiment les titres purs frissons que je n’aime pas comme celui avec les mascottes qui vous foncent dessus. Là il y a vraiment tout une histoire en parallèle et j’aime beaucoup celle-ci. Un jeu qui pourrait être aussi adapté à l’écran, plus via une série qu’un film d’ailleurs.

The story of Prey in 2026 should be divided into two parts: the plot and atmosphere, and the gameplay.
 The main plot is generally at the level of a good science fiction novel, although it is presented very slowly. The side stories are diverse: some are boring, some are interesting (there are more boring ones, but the interesting ones are like REALLY interesting). The lore of the game is revealed through notes, and this is cringe, incredibly boring, and drawn out, but at least it is not necessary: everything that is truly important will be told to you aloud, in plain text, as part of the main story quests. The atmosphere of the game is perfectly conveyed: exploring the space station is scary, interesting, and the locations are memorable. Especially in the first half of the game, when the gameplay is still fresh, the game does a particularly good job of immersing you.
 The gameplay... oh... don't get me wrong, it's not bad, but for this kind of gameplay, the game takes too, too long. At the beginning, the player is not yet familiar with the behavior of the aliens, and they want to explore this cool perk, check out that mysterious location, find a better weapon, and all of this pushes them forward, making them immerse themselves in the game. But hours later, I've already seen all the aliens, I've leveled up all the interesting perks, I've explored all the locations, and I feel like it's time to move on to the ending, but it's still not happening. I want to know how it ends, but I'm being sent back to fix some airlock, carry some ♥♥♥♥ to the other end of the station, explore a location I've already been to, and so on. In short, the game is starting to annoy me.
Overall, I think the game is generally good, but I wouldn't call it a masterpiece. It's up to you whether to buy it or not.

This is one of those games where the space station is basically the main character. Talos I feels huge, strange, expensive, dangerous, and full of secrets someone definitely should have cleaned up before inviting employees to work there.

What I love most is the freedom. It’s not just “go here and shoot that.” You can hack, sneak, climb, repair, recycle, use powers, stack random objects like an idiot with a physics degree, or find some weird route the game quietly allows because Arkane apparently trusts players with bad ideas. That’s the good immersive sim stuff.

The Mimics are also great. After a while you start looking at every coffee mug like it owes you money. A room full of normal office objects becomes more stressful than it has any right to be, which is honestly impressive.

The atmosphere, exploration, GLOO cannon, upgrades, audio logs, and little stories around the station all work together really well. It’s smart, tense, creepy, and rewards curiosity. If you like games that let you solve problems your own way, this is absolutely worth playing.

Просто великолепно. С точки зрения геймдизайна: после пролога игрок волен делать всё, что душе угодно. Абсолютно всё. Игра тебя ни в чем не ограничивает. Вся станция "Талос-1" ближе к концу, когда ты уже освоился и перестал шугаться каждого звука, становится твоей песочницей. Можно обколоться Нейромодами с тифоновскими способностями и кошмарить (pun intended) всю станцию, а можно ни разу к ним не притронуться и пройти игру как самый обычный чел с улицы.

Кстати, о шугании. Первые часов 16 мне было дико страшно. Я буквально боялась каждого шороха.  [spoiler] Молчу про Кошмар. Меня ужасала сама мысль того, что за мной будет бегать огромное гавкающее чучело. К концу игры уже было понятно что ему со мной не тягаться[/spoiler]  Саундтрек, когда в локации находились тифоны, сводил меня с ума, да так, что хотелось выключить игру и убежать. Звуковой дизайн тифонов тоже удался на славу. Даже под конец игры их жуткие непонятные фразы и топот меня напрягали.

Сюжет предельно прост: нашу дорогую станцию "Талос-1" на орбите Луны заполонили инопланетные твари. Надо что-то с этим делать, попутно разбираясь кто мы, что мы тут делаем, и что надо делать дальше. Еще можно следить за тем, как до катастрофы проходили жизни других членов экипажа, да и в целом вся жизнь на борту.

Визуал завораживает. Так как в по лору игры Советский Союз мало того, что не распался, а еще и начал совместно с США работать над космической программой, то интерьеры и плакаты в игре стараются передать дух кооперации между этими двумя странами. Но в основном мне это сильно напомнило стиль Ар Деко. Также еще радует дизайн самих персонажей, тут не найдешь миловидных мордашек, обитатели "Талос-1" выглядят довольно гротескно, с угловатыми и ассиметричными чертами лица, но это придает им этакий шарм.

Я очень рада, что дала этой игре второй шанс (в 2020 моя психика просто не выдержала, и я удалила игру). Полный восторг.

This game has been my #1 game of all time since it released. It is not only one of the most visually stunning games to ever exist (art deco in space by the people who made Dishonored?!?!?!?!?) it is one of the most mechanically satisfying games to ever exist. Its a game that truly has multiple solutions to any problem, take a random door blocking your way, you can hack it, you can use a vent to bypass it, you can use a power to fit through a small opening in the nearby window, use a foam bolt shooting crossbow through that opening to hit the doors release button, or even go off somewhere else to find the doors code. All of those are actual solutions to getting into a single room in the game so imagine how the combat is with stealth mechanics, projectile weapons, throwables that stun lure and disintegrate, beam weapons, stun weapons, all with a boatload of fancy abilities must feel. The story is both one of this games greatest strengths and one of its only pain points as it is fantastically written and engaging but it does have flaws and due to the absurdly freeform nature of everything else the limits of branching quests do pale in comparison. But to be clear it still has meaningful choice in the direction of the story and the story is phenomenal, it is a game where I am excited to listen to every audiolog, to read every note, to read all 6 volumes of an in universe novel (one page a book) that has no real bearing on the story purely because it brings me into the story and its world. 

Prey is a masterpiece like no other and I've reccomended it to near everyone I know!

One of the best immersive sims. For fans of Dishonored and Bioshock, Prey plays like a blend of the two in a very cool near-future sci-fi setting. The visuals still look great years later, the gameplay is extremely smooth and responsive, and the level and ability design does a phenomenal job of giving the player tons of interesting ways to solve every challenge. There are also multiple endings which feel realistically integrated into the world and story. I almost never replay games (and I don't even finish them all that often) but Prey is a game that I have beat multiple times in the past and still plan to beat more than once in the future, due to just how many different ways there are to play it. Plus the roguelike secondary mode, Mooncrash, which is also a ton of fun and is a great way to mix up the gameplay loop for fans who have played the campaign to death. Overall it's one of the best games in the genre and stands out as an extremely underrated gem.

Pros: 
Interesting setting

Solid art direction

Engaging story and extremely detailed world (so many little easter eggs and bits of lore to find!) Lots of weapon and item variety

Side missions that actually take advantage of backtracking in an interesting way

Actually did a cool [spoiler]“it was all a simulation” ending [/spoiler]

When it works, it works well

Cons:
Frustrating intro and first 2 hours, especially with how abundant mimics are before you get the scanner.

Feels like stealth should be an option, but it often isn’t. Almost never gives you the freedom to do important tasks in stealth, and enemy sightlines feel inconsistent and unpredictable.

Some really annoying encounters like the nightmare, who you need to just wait out, and telepaths who have awful pathfinding, a symptom of the overall terrible ai. Not to mention respawning enemies. 

It’s fine that combat is difficult, but you feel much more sluggish than your enemies made worse by how buggy weapon switching can be.

Feels like a significant step back from dishonored, and actually gives you less freedom in enemy encounters despite the open-ended map and abundance of weapons and items.

All of the fun powers are locked behind a path that has massive drawbacks and makes you have to deal with tedious enemy encounters more consistently.

Some great high moments, but the low moments make it feel like a slog.

It did some things great. But I can't get over it's shortcomings, especially when contrasted with Arkane's other works.

I tried 3 times to finish Prey and on my 3rd approach finally it clicked. Prey is an amazing game. It is system shock but brand new and full of references both to Dishonored and Bioshock. Basic gameplay is exploration, resource management and fighting but where the game shines is in letting you do everything your way. The replayability even within ones own playthrough is amazing. I found myself many times deciding to take completely different path/objective because I failed on the one I was trying to achieve, I was rewarded each time with new loot, ability or idea to solve my problems. GAMEPLAY HERE IS KING.

What was wrong that I had to start 3 times?

A bit confusing UI, lack of initial attachment to the story, poor understanding of resource management mechanic.

What tip I would give to someone wanting to play?

You can start fabricating your own ability points early in the game. Love your fabricator - Trust me.

Should you play it if you don't like horrors?

Yes... it's only horror for the first 2 hours then you start to understand what you're dealing with. It's worth it if you like the space setting because this is probably my top 3 space games now.

Prey is one of those games that's just solid all around. The graphics still hold up pretty well imo and Talos 1 has a really immersive atmosphere. The OST isn’t anything super memorable, but it does a great job setting that eerie vibe, especially when ur wandering empty hallways waiting for a mimic to jumpscare u lol.

Gameplay is good overall. Combat can feel kinda basic at times and the RPG mechanics aren’t super deep either, but exploration is fun even if the backtracking gets a little annoying later on. Enemy variety is also kinda lacking, same with the weapons, unless u decide to lean heavily into typhoon powers.

The story is pretty interesting and there’s some nice environmental storytelling too. Dialogue is decent and there’s some player choice involved, but honestly it feels like the game never fully reaches its full potential narratively. The ending especially left me a bit mixed. It’s not bad, but it kinda makes it feel like some of ur choices and sacrifices didn’t really matter in the end. Maybe that was intentional, idk, but it still felt a little unsatisfying.

Performance-wise the game still has some optimization issues. Didn’t run into many bugs or glitches, but I did get random fps drops into the 40-50 range for a few mins at a time which definitely hurt the experience.

Overall tho, Prey is still absolutely worth playing despite its flaws. Best way I can describe it is: jack of all trades, master of none. Everything it does, it does well enough, but nothing really feels peak. Still a really good game tho.

Yea. It's okay. Not as good as Bioshock and entertaining for a lil bit but gets extremely repetitive after a certain point. Environments and enemies start to just repeat themselves. There's about 3 enemy types for you to fight: melee guys that charge at you, flying guys, and other guys which speedhack and use cheats to launch BS at you), and they all just blur together after a while. 
At about 60% through the game it just started becoming a chore with little left in the ship to engage me to want to keep playing. Most enemies could be killed with the shotgun or the psychic blast power, but it wasn't fun at that point as the game just kept throwing enemies at you with more health but shrank the amount of resources and upgrades provided you. I honestly didn't want to keep going at that point because even 12 hours in I'd already unlocked most of the important stuff and there wasn't anything left to pull me in. Just more long grey corridors shooting the same blob enemy type again. It really needed something to break up the monotony in it. Bioshock 1 was great because it respawned enemies in the maps so there was a constant threat and method of farming. In this you'll spend alot of time meticulously managing your inventory to recycle to make a few bits of ammo or neuromods (upgrades). It became tedious before long and I hated that they put in 'secrets' and quests for you to have to backtrack to different areas of the ship. I never went back to the main lobby area or the previous areas for quests as it was just a waste of time.

Overall ok, but it really needed something to halfway to come in and break up the gameplay.

Сюжет:
Интересная и атмосферная история на космической станции с неожиданными поворотами. Тема знакомая, но подача свежая благодаря детальным аудиодневникам и раскрытию через окружение.

Отличный баланс между стелсом и экшеном. Возможность чинить турели, использовать разные способности и подходы к врагам даёт свободу выбора и делает процесс насыщенным.

Атмосфера / Визуал / Звук:
Лучший элемент игры — напряжённая и живописная атмосфера станции. Звуки, освещение и дизайн создают чувство настоящего sci-fi хоррора.

Новизна / Душа:
Несмотря на знакомую тематику, игра наполнена уникальными деталями и живым миром, что удерживает интерес на протяжении всего прохождения.

Минусы:
Иногда встречаются затянутые моменты и небольшая предсказуемость сюжета, но это не портит общего впечатления.

Another game knocked off my Steam Library in 2026, Prey was surprisingly good sci-fi Arkane game set on a space station orbiting earth. It pretty much follows a similar formula to Dishonored where you complete objectives in a variety of ways considering how you've levelled up your character along the way. Skill trees are split between essential human skills and alien abilities, dictating the way how you complete particular tasks.

There's a lot of back and forth traversing the station but the lift (elevator) between the main three sections makes this a lot easier. Space walks are a bit slow and the objective markers could've been better in directing you where to go but apart from those two tiny gripes I had a pretty good time completing the game.

Get it on sale or in a bundle somewhere and you won't go wrong.
